svg.title: Evidence-gated hierarchical scientific memory architecture for MedScience
svg.desc: A publication-quality architecture diagram showing context-aware memory routing, three-tier hierarchical memory, scope-specific subtree mounts for agents, and evidence-gated memory consolidation.
svg.text: Ontology-guided subtree retrieval for reading; verified evidence and versioned claims for durable writeback

g.text: Research plan, stage and active constraints
Active hypothesis branch Hi and agent role a
Privacy, consent, data-locality and ACL scope

svg.text: multi-label routing; not a single hard taxonomy
R(m|q,a,t) = semantic + lexical + graph + evidence − conflict
route decision + retrieval trace are auditable
tree traversal · temporal/version filter · access control · token-budget allocation
Scientific policy · user/project goal · stable preferences
WORKING & EPISODIC MEMORY · SESSION / BRANCH TTL
current plan · recent observations · temporary calculations
branch-local scratch state · compaction summary · unresolved actions
Every node: provenance · valid-time · confidence · scope · version · status
SEMANTIC NAMESPACE AXIS: project → domain/entity/hypothesis/method/open issue
returns a bounded, role-aware view Va,Hᵢ,t; never mounts the full archive

g.text: e.g., molecular biology, clinical evidence, statistics
isolated evidence scope for a competing hypothesis

svg.text: raw EHR/DICOM never enters external model context without explicit consent
Evidence-gated consolidation: the only durable write path
Agents cannot directly write durable scientific memory; every persistent update passes the admission gate.

g.text: candidate memory must pass all applicable tests

svg.text: evidence is immutable; claims are versioned; memory is a derived, auditable and revocable view—not the source of truth.
